prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
Labour Party Manifesto 2024 – Summary (≤500 words)

Core theme: Change. End “Conservative chaos,” restore trust, and begin national renewal with mission‑driven government built on strong foundations: national security, secure borders, and economic stability.

Five national missions
- Kickstart growth: Highest sustained G7 growth; pro‑business and pro‑worker “securonomics”; stable fiscal rules (no rises to NI, Income Tax rates or VAT); abolish non‑dom status, close tax loopholes, modernise HMRC.
- Clean energy superpower: Zero‑carbon electricity by 2030; Great British Energy (publicly owned, £8.3bn) to co‑invest; double onshore wind, triple solar, quadruple offshore wind; new nuclear (Hinkley, Sizewell C, SMRs); no new North Sea exploration licences (honour existing); extend tougher windfall tax; £6.6bn Warm Homes Plan to upgrade 5m homes; tougher water regulation and nature recovery.
- Take back our streets: Neighbourhood Policing Guarantee with thousands more officers/PCSOs; Respect Orders for antisocial behaviour; specific offence for assaults on shopworkers; halve knife crime in a decade with mandatory interventions and bans on zombie-style blades; specialist rape units and courts; policing vetting standards; fraud strategy; rebuild prisons capacity, cut reoffending.
- Break down barriers to opportunity: 6,500 new teachers funded by ending private school tax breaks; free breakfast clubs in every primary; 3,000 school‑based nurseries; curriculum and assessment reform; mental health support in every school; Skills England; replace Apprenticeship Levy with flexible Growth & Skills Levy; Technical Excellence Colleges; renters’ reform (end Section 21, raise standards), leasehold abolition pathway; child poverty reduction strategy; equality package (Race Equality Act, disability/ethnicity pay gap reporting, ban conversion practices).
- Build an NHS fit for the future: 40,000 extra weekly appointments (evenings/weekends), shared waiting lists, use of independent sector; double CT/MRI scanners; deliver New Hospitals Programme; transform NHS app; more GPs, face‑to‑face guarantee, continuity of “family doctor”; expand pharmacy prescribing and self‑referrals; Neighbourhood Health Centres; Dentistry Rescue Plan (700k urgent appointments, contract reform, supervised tooth‑brushing); National Care Service with national standards and a Fair Pay Agreement in adult social care; 8,500 extra mental health staff; strong public health measures (smoking and youth vaping curbs, junk food ad limits).

Economy, business, infrastructure and housing
- Industrial strategy with a statutory Industrial Strategy Council; National Wealth Fund (£7.3bn) to crowd in private capital (ports, gigafactories, steel, CCUS, hydrogen).
- Tax certainty: cap corporation tax at 25% for the parliament; permanent full expensing; replace business rates in England.
- 10‑year infrastructure strategy; National Infrastructure and Service Transformation Authority; rail brought into public ownership as contracts end; EV transition support; restore 2030 ICE phase‑out; bus franchising and municipal ownership options; nationwide gigabit/5G by 2030; Regulatory Innovation Office; binding rules for frontier AI.
- Build 1.5m homes: restore targets; brownfield‑first plus strategic “grey belt” release under “golden rules”; new towns; more social and affordable homes; permanent mortgage guarantee for first‑time buyers.

Borders, security and governance
- Border Security Command; more caseworkers to clear asylum backlog; end Rwanda scheme and hotel use; faster returns.
- Defence: unwavering NATO and nuclear deterrent; Strategic Defence Review; path to 2.5% of GDP; defence industrial strategy; steadfast support for Ukraine and AUKUS; balanced China approach.
- Political reform: Ethics and Integrity Commission; ban MPs’ paid consultancy roles; Commons modernisation; Lords immediate reforms (end hereditary peers, retirement at 80) and consult on replacement; votes at 16; reset devolution relationships; Council of the Nations and Regions.

Foreign policy and development
- Make Brexit work: better EU trade in targeted areas (veterinary deal, qualifications), UK‑EU security pact; targeted global trade strategy; Clean Power Alliance; restore 0.7% aid when fiscally possible; rebuild development expertise.

Fiscal approach
- Strict fiscal rules; fully costed measures; savings from halving consultancy spend, ending Rwanda scheme/hotel use, and other efficiencies fund frontline priorities.
